description: Second flight article of the first Buran series (serial 2K 11F35); intended name Burya; widely known abroad as Ptichka; assessed at 95-97 percent complete when the programme was closed in 1993; survived the 2002 collapse because it was stored in the blast-resistant fuelling building at Site 112A; photographed inside by blogger Ralph Mirebs in 2015; vandalised with graffiti by intruders in 2021 after which the hangar was placed under 24-hour guard and the paint removed; ownership is Kazakh-private — AO RKK Baikonur holds it with Dauren Musa owning 80 percent and state company Infrakos 20 percent; a 2019 Kazakh state suit sought to liquidate the company and return the orbiter to state ownership
museum_name: Buran Assembly and Fuelling Building -- Baikonur Site 112A

description: Technological mock-up of the Buran orbiter (izdeliye 0.15; 11F35MT 4MT) built for pre-launch procedure development including fit and handling trials with the Energia launch vehicle; delivered to Baikonur 1984 and used in testing until 1990; stored alongside Buran 1.02 in the fuelling building at Site 112A; stated in Russian sources to be the property of Kazakhstan
museum_name: Buran Assembly and Fuelling Building -- Baikonur Site 112A
